source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Microeconomics, Ch. 1 (Introduction).

sections.heading: 1. The Economic Problem — Scarcity and Choice
points: The central economic problem = **scarcity** — **unlimited wants vs limited (scarce) resources** with alternative uses → the need to **choose**.
Every choice has an **opportunity cost** — the value of the next-best alternative given up.
Economics studies how societies allocate scarce resources.

sections.heading: 2. Central Problems of an Economy

sub: **How to produce** (which technique — labour or capital intensive)?

points: Also: **how to use resources fully and efficiently, and how to grow (raise capacity over time)**.

sections.heading: 3. Production Possibility Frontier (PPF)
points: The **Production Possibility Frontier (PPF)/Curve** shows the **maximum combinations of two goods** an economy can produce with given resources and technology.
It is **concave (bowed outward)** due to increasing opportunity cost; the **slope = Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC)**.
Points **on** the PPF = efficient/full use; **inside** = inefficient/unemployed resources; **outside** = unattainable (unless resources/technology grow → PPF shifts out).

sections.heading: 4. Types of Economies
points: **Market economy** — decisions by the price mechanism (demand and supply).
**Centrally planned (command) economy** — the government decides.
**Mixed economy** — both market and government (like India).
Microeconomics studies individual decision-making; macroeconomics the whole economy.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Economic problem = scarcity (unlimited wants, limited resources) → choice.
Opportunity cost = value of the next-best alternative forgone.
Central problems: what, how, and for whom to produce.
PPF = max combinations of two goods; concave (increasing opportunity cost).
Economies: market, centrally planned, mixed (India).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Scarcity + choice** is the central economic problem; every choice has an **opportunity cost**.
The **PPF is concave** (increasing opportunity cost); its slope = **Marginal Opportunity Cost**.
Points **inside** the PPF = **inefficient/unemployed** resources.
Central problems: **what, how, and for whom** to produce.
